players.product: High-complexity multilayer PCBs, substrates and advanced packaging for AI data-center/networking systems

quarterly_data.signal: Q4 FY2025 RESULTS (CEO Edwin Roks, CFO Dan Bailey): Q4 net sales were $774.3 million versus $651 million a year earlier, up 19% year over year and 'above the high end of our guided range', driven by data center computing, networking, medical/industrial/instrumentation and aerospace and defense, partly offset by a decline in automotive. Non-GAAP EPS of $0.70 per diluted share met the high end of guidance and was 'an all-time quarterly record high'. Q4 adjusted EBITDA was $126.2 million, 16.3% of net sales, versus 14.7% a year earlier; non-GAAP operating margin was 12.7%, 'a 260 basis points improvement from 10.1% in the same quarter last year', on the gross-margin improvement (higher sales volume, favorable data center computing/networking and A&D mix, improved operational execution) and continued SG&A spending discipline. Full-year 2025 net sales were $2.9 billion versus $2.4 billion (+19%), with adjusted EBITDA of $456.3 million (15.7% of net sales) and cash flow from operations of $292 million (10% of sales).
quarterly_data.figure: Q4 net sales $774.3 million (+19% YoY); non-GAAP EPS $0.70 (all-time quarterly record); adjusted EBITDA 16.3% vs 14.7%; FY2025 net sales $2.9 billion vs $2.4 billion

quarterly_data.signal: Q1 FY2026 GUIDANCE AND 2026 OUTLOOK (CFO, CEO): net sales of $770 million to $810 million and non-GAAP EPS of $0.64 to $0.70 per diluted share (the transcript prints 'for 2026'; the CFO then calls it the first quarter 2026 EPS forecast, on about 106.7 million diluted shares), with Q1 profitability typically hit by higher labor costs around the Chinese New Year holiday. Full-year 2026 total net sales are expected to increase 15% to 20% over 2025. The CEO said TTM is on track for its ambition, first shared on January 13, to grow revenues 15% to 20% per year for the next three years and to double earnings from 2025 to 2027, and that 'This is all organic growth. Because there is so much demand, and we are investing in our capacity.'
quarterly_data.figure: Q1 2026 net sales $770 million to $810 million, non-GAAP EPS $0.64 to $0.70; FY2026 net sales +15% to 20% over 2025

quarterly_data.signal: AI DRIVES DATA CENTER COMPUTING AND NETWORKING (CEO): data center computing was 20% of Q4 2025 sales, growing 57% year over year in the quarter and 36% for full-year 2025, 'which reflects continued demand strength from our data center customers building products for AI applications.' Networking grew 23% year over year in Q4 and 43% for the full year 'as this market continues to become more correlated with the AI-related demand for more complex switching technology' (the transcript prints networking at 8% of 2025 sales). Because of that AI correlation the two will be reported as one combined data center and networking end market from 2026 (four end markets in total): combined, they would have been 36% of 2025 sales, and they are expected to be 37% of Q1 2026 sales.
quarterly_data.figure: Data center computing 20% of Q4 sales, +57% YoY (FY2025 +36%); networking +23% YoY in Q4 (FY2025 +43%); combined 36% of 2025 sales, 37% expected in Q1 2026

quarterly_data.signal: A&D, SPACE, MI&I AND AUTOMOTIVE (CEO): aerospace and defense was 41% of Q4 2025 sales, growing 5% year over year in the quarter and 13% for full-year 2025 on defense budget tailwinds, program alignment and key bookings; 2025 bookings included the APS-153 airborne surveillance radar, LTAMDS air defense radar, MRAM, air dominance missile and Javelin anti-armor missile system, plus more restricted programs. A&D book-to-bill was 1.46 for the quarter and 1.04 for the year, lifting program backlog to $1.6 billion from $1.56 billion a year ago; that backlog generally runs 'two years or even two and a half years' and 'The pipeline is even bigger.' A&D is expected to be 42% of Q1 2026 sales. Space is 'absolutely one of our strategic directions' that TTM is working on now, needing more PCBs and also integrated modules and radiation-hard products. Medical, industrial and instrumentation was 14% of Q4 sales (+28% year over year; +22% for 2025) on AI-enabled robotics, more complex sensing and automated testing equipment, and is expected to be 14% of 2026 sales. Automotive was 9% of Q4 sales and is expected at about 8% of 2026 sales, with TTM 'increasingly selective' toward higher value-add products.
quarterly_data.figure: A&D 41% of Q4 sales (+5% YoY), book-to-bill 1.46, program backlog $1.6 billion, 42% of Q1 2026 sales expected; MI&I 14% (+28%); automotive 9%, about 8% in 2026

quarterly_data.signal: ORDERS AND VISIBILITY (CEO): overall book-to-bill was 1.35 (the transcript prints 'for 2025'), with the A&D reporting segment at 1.46 and the RF&S reporting segment at 0.94. The 90-day backlog, subject to cancellations, was $654.9 million at the end of 2025 versus $502.1 million a year earlier. Asked whether the strong commercial orders reflected customers locking in capacity, the CEO said visibility on the running commercial business, 'mostly data centers and networking', has not changed: 'it's still about six to nine months. That's our outlook, which is a normal number.' He expects more visibility over time on 'some more strategic elements of the same customers.'
quarterly_data.figure: book-to-bill 1.35 (A&D 1.46, RF&S 0.94); 90-day backlog $654.9 million vs $502.1 million; commercial visibility about six to nine months

quarterly_data.signal: CHINA AI-BOARD CAPACITY AND 2026 CAPEX (CFO, CEO): the data center and compute capacity being added in China carries 'an additional incremental capital expenditure of about $200 to $300 million over the next two to three years', above TTM's '4% to 5% normal capital expenditures'. The CFO said the 10-K would disclose expected 2026 capex 'in the range of $240 to $260 million', at 'almost the same level' going into the next year and growing into the following year. Dongguan and Guangzhou are the two sites where TTM makes its artificial intelligence boards now; the China spend is additional equipment, facilitation and optimization of lines in those same factories - 'it's not new factories' - so the new capacity can be brought up 'very easily and efficiently'. The CEO said the capacity being added covers the 15% to 20% growth plan, and 'we have even more capacity to do even more depending on the demand.'
quarterly_data.figure: about $200 to $300 million incremental China data-center capex over the next two to three years; 2026 capex $240 to $260 million

quarterly_data.signal: PENANG AND SYRACUSE RAMPS (CFO, CEO): Penang (Malaysia) was still about a 180 basis point headwind at the gross profit level in Q4, worse than the 160 guided, and should fall to about half of that by the end of the year. The CEO said 'We basically doubled the revenues versus last quarter' at Penang, yields on the lead vehicles are moving in the right direction, and he hopes to do 'a lot better' than halving the headwind. Q4 gross margin still improved, primarily on data center and networking mix and then better A&D margins. Syracuse is on track: lead customers are in place, the building is up, the equipment is in, and TTM will see first revenues from Syracuse in the second half of this year.
quarterly_data.figure: Penang gross-profit headwind about 180 basis points in Q4 (160 guided), to about half by year-end; Syracuse first revenues in the second half of this year

quarterly_data.signal: EAU CLAIRE - THE LARGEST PCB SITE IN THE US (CEO): the Eau Claire site, whose previous owner was TDK, is 'the largest PCB site in the US' (excluding some customers' in-house activities) at 750,000 square feet across three different modules. TTM will tool up the facility over the coming eighteen months to two years and is discussing the plan with lead customers on both the commercial and the defense side - 'They need the capacity.' First revenues are about eighteen to twenty-four months away. The CEO added that Eau Claire sits outside the capacity plans already described (the transcript prints 'Eau Claire is not building the capacity plans we described').
quarterly_data.figure: 750,000 square feet; eighteen to twenty-four months to first revenues

quarterly_data.signal: LAYER COUNTS KEEP CLIMBING (CEO): asked about the most advanced AI boards TTM makes (the analyst cited 87-layer asymmetric designs), the CEO corrected the count and pointed to rising complexity: 'Everything beyond the 60 layers... The 78, not the 87. The 78 layers is one of the boards we are working on, and that's going very smooth. But I can tell you that numbers go up.' He added: 'The demand is high. But the number of layers is going up. There are numbers beyond the 100 layers already, which are required. Of course, these systems become more and more compact, which requires more layers and more complexity. And we are well-positioned there.'
quarterly_data.figure: 78 layers on a board in work; customers already requiring beyond the 100 layers

quarterly_data.signal: NO CAPACITY, SUPPLY-CHAIN OR EQUIPMENT CONSTRAINT; COPPER PASSED THROUGH (CEO, CFO): on expanding capacity in China and the US, the CEO said 'capacity is not the issue. Also, the supply chain is not the issue. The equipment is not the issue. So we are well on track.' Asked about volatile, rising copper prices, the CFO said 'We don't expect any significant impacts from it. Generally, we build the volatility into our pricing.' and 'We're able to pass that through to our customers.' TTM also hedges copper, but 'the biggest mitigation is that we're able to price it in.'
